segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now in Antioch, in the assembly there, were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Now set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So these two, sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Arriving in Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John as an assistant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain magician, a Jewish false prophet named Bar-Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Elymas the magician—for that is how his name is translated—opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked straight at him

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You who are full of all deceit and all villainy, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And now look, the hand of the Lord is against you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately mist and darkness fell on him, and he went around looking for people to lead him by the hand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Paul and his companions put out to sea from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John, however, left them and returned to Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they went on from Perga and arrived at Pisidian Antioch. On the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and sat down.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, speak.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Israelites, and you who fear God, listen.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and lifted up the people during their stay as foreigners in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm he led them out of it.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And for about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and after overthrowing seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave their land as an inheritance,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: all of this over about four hundred and fifty years. After that he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: After removing him, he raised up David as their king, and bore witness about him, saying, ‘I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who will carry out all my wishes.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: From this man’s offspring God, as he promised, has brought to Israel a savior, Jesus.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Before his arrival, John had already preached to all the people of Israel a baptism of turning back.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And as John was completing his course, he would say, ‘What do you suppose I am? I am not he. But look, one is coming after me, and I am not worthy to untie the sandals on his feet.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Brothers, sons of Abraham’s family, and those among you who fear God, it is to us that the word of this salvation has been sent.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For the people living in Jerusalem and their rulers, failing to recognize him or to understand the voices of the prophets that are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Though they found no grounds for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have him put to death.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: When they had carried out everything that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But God raised him from the dead,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And we bring you the good news of the promise made to the fathers:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: God has fulfilled it for our children by raising Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm: ‘You are my Son; today I have become your Father.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And as for his raising him from the dead, never again to return to decay, he has spoken in this way: ‘I will give you the holy and faithful things of David.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: That is why he also says in another place, ‘You will not let your Holy One see decay.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For David, after serving God’s purpose in his own generation, fell asleep and was gathered to his fathers and saw decay,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: but the one whom God raised did not see decay.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So let it be known to you, brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and that from everything from which you could not be justified by the Law of Moses,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: by this man everyone who believes is justified.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Take care, then, that what is said in the Prophets does not come upon you:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: ‘Look, you scoffers, be amazed and vanish, for I am doing a work in your days, a work you will never believe even if someone tells you of it.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As Paul and Barnabas were going out, the people begged that these things be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the synagogue meeting had broken up, many of the Jews and the devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke with them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the following Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they contradicted what Paul was saying, hurling insults.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first. Since you thrust it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the end of the earth.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who had been appointed to eternal life believed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the word of the Lord spread through the whole region.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Jews stirred up the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, raised a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their territory.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they shook the dust off their feet against them and went to Iconium.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

notes.note: The traditional rendering is “church.” A first-century hearer knew the word as a gathering of people—a civic assembly, or in the Septuagint Israel assembled before God—whereas “church” now suggests a building or an institution. Nearly all translations keep “church,” which readers readily understand; “assembly” is used here throughout so that the one Greek word stays visible.

Greek has a single word family where English has two: “righteous” and “just,” “righteousness” and “justice,” and the verb “justify.” “Righteousness” is kept here, as in most English translations, though some scholars prefer “justice.” The verb of this family appears in verses 38–39 as “justified,” where “justified from” carries the sense of being cleared of a charge and so released from it.

Besides Jews by birth, synagogues in the Greek cities attracted Gentiles who worshiped Israel’s God and kept some Jewish practices without becoming full converts. Paul addresses them alongside the Israelites here and again in verse 26. How formal or uniform a group these “God-fearers” were is debated.

The manuscripts are divided between two verbs that differ by a single letter: “he put up with them” and “he cared for them,” as a nurse carries a child. The same variation is found in the Greek text of Deuteronomy 1:31, which Paul echoes here. The evidence is closely balanced and translations differ; the text followed here reads “put up with.”

The Greek word translated “nations” here is the same word translated “Gentiles” in verses 46–48. It means a people or nation, and in the plural it often refers to the non-Jewish peoples as a whole. The translation chooses between the two English words according to the sense.

notes.phrase: all of this over about four hundred and fifty years
notes.traditional: and after that he gave them judges for about four hundred and fifty years
notes.note: In the earliest manuscripts the four hundred and fifty years belong with what precedes, apparently covering the stay in Egypt, the wilderness years and the conquest. Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, place the figure after the giving of judges, making it the length of the judges’ period. The words “all of this” make the reference of the earlier reading clear.

The traditional rendering is “repentance,” which most translations keep as an established term understood to include a change of life. In modern English that word centers on feeling sorry, whereas the Greek carries the prophets’ call to return to God: a change of direction in mind and conduct.

The earliest and best manuscripts read “for our children,” which fits the context awkwardly, since Paul is speaking of his own generation. Other manuscripts read “for us, their children” or “for their children,” and many translations adopt “for us, their children.” Some scholars suspect an early copying error behind all the surviving readings.

This may mean raising Jesus from the dead, as the same verb plainly does in verse 34, or raising him up in the sense of bringing him onto the stage of history, as Scripture speaks of God raising up a prophet. Interpreters are divided, and the rendering leaves both possibilities open.

notes.phrase: the holy and faithful things of David
notes.traditional: the sure mercies of David; the holy and sure blessings of David
notes.note: The quotation follows the Greek version of Isaiah 55:3, where the Hebrew speaks of God’s reliable acts of loyal love toward David. The Greek is terse—“the holy things of David, the faithful ones”—and translations usually supply a noun such as “blessings” or “promises.” The plain wording is kept so that the link with “your Holy One” in the next verse, which is the same Greek word, remains visible.

notes.phrase: after serving God’s purpose in his own generation
notes.note: The Greek can be construed in more than one way: “after serving God’s purpose in his own generation,” “after serving his own generation by God’s purpose,” or “after serving his own generation, fell asleep by God’s purpose.” Translations are divided. The contrast with Jesus, who did not see decay, is unaffected.

The traditional rendering is “blaspheming.” In first-century Greek the verb meant abusive or defamatory speech against anyone, not only against God, and no object is stated here; many modern translations have “reviling him” or “heaped abuse on him.” Some interpreters do read it as blasphemy against Christ.

In Jewish usage “eternal life” is the life of the age to come, a matter of its kind as well as its length. “Eternal” is the standard rendering and is kept here; a minority of translators render “the life of the age to come.”

The verb means to assign, arrange or appoint, and the form here is most naturally read as a passive, “had been appointed,” with God as the implied agent; this is the majority view. Some take it instead as “had set themselves” toward eternal life, in contrast to those in verse 46 who judged themselves unworthy of it. The text does not say when or on what basis the appointing took place.

candidates.reason: The same word names the visitors of Matthew 2 (traditionally “magi” or “wise men”) and the court practitioner here, so the New Testament needs one decision on whether and how the English should vary.
The plural for Israel’s forebears recurs across Acts, Paul and Hebrews, and translators split between “fathers” and “ancestors.”
A central term across the New Testament where “grace,” “favor” and “gift” are all defensible and readers would be misled by unexplained variation.
The noun and its verb range over “encouragement,” “exhortation,” “comfort” and “appeal,” and the choice needs to be principled across Acts, Paul and Hebrews.
Used of the cross in Acts, Galatians and 1 Peter with an echo of Deuteronomy 21:23, and of the tree of life in Revelation; “tree,” “wood” and “cross” all appear in translations.
